source.title: Scaling a context-aware genomic model for condition-specific edit design in plants
source.authors: Paride Antinucci; Lin-Feng Wang; Jacob D. Moss; Dennis Schwartz; D. Hall

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Extends scaling-law measurements to a plant genomic expression model trained with supervised prediction, rather than language-model pretraining.
record.gate_note: The paper reports validation-MSE scaling with CROP-1 model size, experiment-data size, and training compute. These results bear on V5 as evidence from a genomic setting. The study does not measure language-model cross-entropy, test small-run extrapolation to much larger runs, or find a compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Its citations to neural scaling studies are not results from this study.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own scaling sweeps (5 model sizes, 5 data sizes) for a supervised genomic CNN, with power-law fits of held-out validation MSE. This bears on V5 (power-law form beyond text pretraining). It tests no language-model pretraining loss, extrapolation, compute-optimal split or shape.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that capacity and experiment-level data scaling reduce validation MSE (by 47.8% and 57.7%) and that both still improve at the largest scales. They say the empirical power laws link to neural scaling, but the fits identify no theoretical regime.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a context-aware convolutional genomic model for supervised gene-expression prediction and validation MSE, not language models, held-out pretraining cross-entropy, or a compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. It varies model size and training-data size and also plots training-compute trajectories.
record.method_sensitivity: The data-scaling results depend on experiment-context subset selection by TF-expression-profile clustering; the subsets have different context coverage and observation counts.

fits_no_version.finding: Test-set tissue- and gene-level Pearson correlations rise with model size in all four generalisation strata (e.g. known/known gene r 0.574→0.756). Experiment-level per-gene r also rises with data (0.291→0.461 for known genes).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Held-out correlation metrics in genomic expression models improve monotonically with model and data scale.

record.problems: The scaling evidence is from one plant genomic expression model and supervised validation MSE, not language-model pretraining cross-entropy. The power-law fits use five points each; no uncertainty for the fit parameters is reported, and training-compute trajectories are not fitted to a power law. The study does not test extrapolation to separately evaluated larger runs.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported findings were omitted; results on context inputs, foundation-model comparisons, fine-tuning, and edit design do not measure the scaling relationships relevant to V5.

untested.parts: Image/video models, repeated-data regimes and power-law scaling of fine-tuning/transfer. The multi-species fine-tuning comparison has no scale sweep. No joint N–D or compute law is fitted.
No prediction of held-out larger runs from small-run fits.
No downstream-task relation to loss or scale.
No comparison of fitting choices or exponents across setups.

missing.what: Converged validation MSE for the 10M, 40M and 100M models, and the stated 7.7% drop from 100M to 400M
Test-set correlation/MSE by model size across the four strata

record.verdict_notes: Supervised CNN with cross-attention, not LM pretraining. Each fit uses five points, with no fit uncertainty reported. The flattening I compute suggests an irreducible-loss term that a pure power law omits. The authors claim continued gains but do not discuss the bend.

versions.untested_parts: No language model or held-out pretraining cross-entropy is measured.
The study fits scaling curves but does not test whether fits on small runs predict separately evaluated runs orders of magnitude larger.
No compute-optimal parameter/token allocation is evaluated.
No comparison of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count is reported.
Tests a plant genomic expression-prediction setting only; it does not test image or video models, repeated-data training, or whether power laws hold for fine-tuning or transfer.
No downstream-task performance relationship with pretraining loss or scale is tested.
The paper does not compare fitting choices or demonstrate that exponents or compute-optimal splits vary with setup; it notes that its fits do not identify a particular theoretical scaling regime.

rows.subject: CROP-1

conditions.value: Common optimiser schedule and global batch size

rows.value: 0.1525 at 400M parameters; 47.8% reduction; losses decreased at every increase in size
rows.locator: Results, “Model scaling systematically improves expression prediction”; Fig. 2b
rows.note: The paper reports a five-configuration empirical power-law fit, with exponent 0.152 and log-space R2 of 0.967; see R2.
rows.check: The text also gives a 7.7% reduction from 100M to 400M. This implies a local exponent of ~0.06, versus the fitted 0.152, so flattening at the top is not captured in the row. Losses for 10M/40M/100M appear only in Fig. 2b.

rows.subject: CROP-1
rows.operation_detail: Expanded experiment-level training data to all eligible observations.
rows.locator: Table 2; Results, “Tissue aggregation and context diversity enable efficient data scaling”
rows.note: The paper reports continued improvement at the largest data scale, including a 4.6% reduction relative to the 50% subset.
rows.check: Loss keeps falling, but only 4.6% for a 1.9× data increase (Table 2). The fitted αD=0.192 implies about 12%. The local exponent falls from ~0.34 (1%→5%) to ~0.07 (50%→100%), so the curve flattens.

relationships.condition: CROP-1 supervised plant expression prediction; model size 4M–400M and experiment-data 7.8M–568M observations, each run trained to convergence
relationships.reason: Validation MSE falls monotonically. Single-term power laws fit with log-space R²=0.967 (αN=0.152) and 0.924 (αD=0.192) (R1, R2, R4–R8).
relationships.display_finding: Validation MSE decreased monotonically, with model-size fits giving αN=0.152 and log-space R²=0.967 and data fits giving αD=0.192 and log-space R²=0.924.

relationships.reason: Gains at the top are much smaller than the fitted exponents imply: 7.7% vs ~19% expected, and 4.6% vs ~12% expected. Local exponents fall steadily, so the single power law bends (R1, R6, R7). This is computed from the study's numbers, not stated by the authors.
relationships.display_finding: Calculated parameter and data gains were 7.7% versus about 19% expected and 4.6% versus about 12% expected, with steadily declining local exponents.

relationships.reason: Data subsets are non-nested clustering selections that also change context diversity. Data size is therefore confounded with composition, and the authors say composition matters (R3–R8).
relationships.display_finding: Non-nested clustering selections changed context diversity alongside dataset size, confounding data volume with composition.
